snippet.title: Génération Z : habiter le monde autrement | Elisabeth Soulié | TEDxSaclay
snippet.description: La génération Z, déroute. Née au tournant du millénaire, Social Native, qui  est-elle vraiment? Pourquoi bouscule-t-elle à ce point les schémas de pensée des générations précédentes? Comprendre ses comportements, ses représentations et ses attentes n’est-ce pas une nécessité pour apprendre à vivre ensemble et  ne pas manquer le rendez-vous avec le monde qui vient ? Anthropologue diplômée de l’Ecole des Hautes Etudes en Sciences Sociales (EHESS) et coach formée à Metasystème, Elisabeth Soulié développe son expertise de la génération Z au travers de terrains ethnographiques et de publics très divers: en Seine Saint-Denis au coeur d’un lycée professionnel, au sein d’un institut de santé  en zone rurale, à Paris et en province auprès de collectifs de jeunes activistes, dans des tiers-lieu de travail et incubateurs de start-up. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

snippet.title: Systems Falling Apart? This Might Be Why #ADHD #LifeHacks #SurvivalMode
snippet.description: Systems that aren't working on your worst brain days... may not be the right system for you... or it isn't simplified enough. Because, here's the thing, systems that work when you have time and energy aren't going to work when you don't have time... or energy... (or god forbid, both). For some systems that may be totally fine... but for those systems that are critical for us to function? It's important to simplify these systems so that they can still work when we don't have time... or energy.... or both! #short

snippet.title: Does CBT Work for Autistic People? A Therapist Explains
snippet.description:
There is a common belief that Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT) “doesn’t work” for autistic people. The reality is far more nuanced. In this clear and detailed exploration, CBT Therapist Laura Oates explains when CBT can be effective, when it might not be the right approach, and how it can be adapted to support autistic clients.

Laura explores:
• What CBT actually is — and what it aims to change
• Why CBT helps with anxiety, depression and stress for many people
• The wide variability within autism and why generalisations don’t work
• How autistic and neurotypical clients differ in therapy needs
• When CBT is not suitable (for autistic or neurotypical clients)
• How therapists tailor sessions to the individual
• Research showing CBT can work for autistic young people
• The importance of insight, motivation and communication in any CBT process
• Practical adaptations for autistic clients (concrete language, structure, sensory considerations, behavioural focus, worksheets, and more)
• How CBT can also support social skills, emotional regulation, independence and executive function
• Whether an autistic therapist is necessary (and why therapeutic alliance matters most)
• What to ask when choosing a therapist experienced with neurodivergent clients

This is a balanced, supportive guide for autistic individuals, parents, partners or anyone considering CBT as an option.

About Laura Oates
Laura Oates is a Cognitive Behavioural Therapist experienced in working with autistic and neurodivergent clients struggling with anxiety, depression, executive functioning challenges and relationship difficulties. She tailors CBT to each person’s strengths, sensory needs and communication style.

snippet.title: Courage Is the New Authority | Markus Eilers | TEDxTUDarmstadt
snippet.description:
A talk about finding authority through courage, clear communication, and the willingness to show up authentically. Markus Eilers once lived the life of a content software architect — until the financial crisis forced him into the unknown. Practically overnight, the world he had built collapsed, and he had to confront something he’d always avoided: approaching strangers, starting conversations, persuading.

That uncomfortable necessity became a revelation. Markus realised that communication is not just a skill — it’s survival, it’s growth, it’s the bridge that carries ideas into the world.

Today, his greatest joy is helping others step beyond their fears and discover that authority doesn’t come from titles, but from the courage to connect. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

snippet.title: US trade official elaborates on CUSMA grievances after rejecting deal's renewal
snippet.description:

The agreement covers roughly $2.5 trillion in trade annually. U.S. President Donald Trump negotiated the deal himself during his first term, calling it one of the fairest and most balanced of its kind at the time.

CUSMA will expire on July 1st, 2036, or earlier if one of the three countries gives six months’ notice of withdrawal.

snippet.title: Je suis devenu aidant....sans le savoir. | Vincent VALINDUCQ | TEDxSaclay
snippet.description: Pendant 14 ans, Vincent Valinducq est devenu le parent de ses parents. Entre fatigue, culpabilité et amour, il nous raconte, avec justesse et parfois humour, son histoire bouleversante. Un témoignage puissant et utile pour comprendre qu'aider les autres commence par ne pas s'oublier soi-même. Originaire du Havre, Vincent Valinducq, ancien ouvrier docker, est médecin généraliste à Paris depuis plus de 11 ans. Chroniqueur santé dans Bonjour la matinale sur TF1, il vulgarise la médecine au grand public. Auteur de « Je suis devenu le parent de mes parents », il s’engage pour les aidants. En 2026, il devient vice-président de la Fondation Médéric Alzheimer. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

snippet.title: The Best Career Advice for Right Now: The New Rules of Work, Confidence, and Success
snippet.description:
If work feels shaky right now:
If you’re being overlooked for a promotion or raise, 
If you’re changing jobs or looking for a job,
If you’ve been feeling uneasy about changes in tech and AI,
If the feeling at work is “anything could happen…” 

This episode is for you.

The world is moving fast, companies are shifting, and a lot of people are sitting back and hoping they don’t get hit. 

Carla Harris is here to make sure you’re not one of them.

Carla is one of the most respected leaders on Wall Street. She’s spent 35 years in the rooms where decisions get made: who gets promoted, who gets picked, who gets overlooked, and why. 

The world is changing fast. The strategies that worked in 2025 will not work in 2026.
When the world changes, you must change with it, or as our expert will caution you – you’ll “become a fossil.”

She will tell you exactly which skills, what mindset, and what actions you need to take in 2026 to succeed at work so you can position yourself so you’re not waiting for someone else to “notice” your potential.

In this conversation, you will learn:
-The 2 things holding women back at any stage in their career and how to overcome them
-How to stand out at work in the age of AI and nonstop change
-How to take control of your career in midlife (It’s easier than you think)
-The one relationship that gets you promoted (and it’s not always your boss)
-What to do when you’re exhausted but still need to show up and perform
-How to finally stop self-doubt (without any weird tricks or hacks)
-How to evolve your career without starting from scratch
-How to prepare for your annual review so you get what you want
-Why you can be great at your job and still get overlooked (and what to do about it)
-How to figure out what you want next using Carla’s “blank sheet” method
-How to build a timeline to escape a toxic job without blowing up your life

You’ll also hear Carla coach real listeners through layoffs, rebuilding confidence, and returning to work after years at home.

Carla calls this next chapter Me 3.0. This is the phase where you stop living by someone else’s report card and start designing a career (and life) you want to wake up for.

Today, she’s giving you the career coaching session of a lifetime – one that no amount of money could buy, because she doesn’t offer one on one sessions.

She says, this is not the moment to sit back – it’s time to put your foot on the gas.

snippet.title: Weird Habits That Reveal High Intelligence
snippet.description:
Do you have some "weird" habits that make you wonder if you’re a bit odd? As it turns out, being "normal" isn't the only benchmark for being smart. Many of history’s most brilliant minds were known for their quirks. In this video, we explore the psychology behind behaviors that might seem strange on the surface but are actually indicators of a sharp, creative, and highly intelligent mind.

In this video, I break down why that happens and one practical way to build a healthier sense of self.

Why is it so hard to stay organized with ADHD? And is disorganization actually a symptom of ADHD?

Psychologist Dr. Monica Johnson answers the internet’s biggest questions on ADHD and organization. She explains how executive function skills like planning, prioritizing, working memory, and task initiation are essential parts of organization. snippet.description:
If you keep ending up in the same relationship dynamic, it’s not bad luck.

Your brain is drawn to what feels familiar—even when it isn’t healthy.

This is called repetition compulsion: repeating early attachment patterns without realizing it.

The shift starts when you recognize the pattern.

Sometimes healthy will feel unfamiliar, even boring. That’s not a lack of chemistry—it’s a lack of chaos.

snippet.title: Healthcare isn’t a privilege, it’s a human right | Zenishah Zenishah Gogri | TEDxDAA Youth
snippet.description: When was the last time you saw a doctor without checking your bank account first?  Our world has put a price tag on survival, your life is worth exactly what you can afford. But how much is that "marketing force" actually costing us in human lives? In this talk, Zenishah explores the Healthcare Composite Readiness Score, a personalized blueprint designed to dismantle the barriers of every economic reality. From leveraging the wealth of the global elite to addressing the structural barriers that keep a single mother from a clinic, she reveals how we can stop treating healthcare as a privilege and finally start treating it as a fundamental human right. Zenishah is a Grade 9 student from India with a profound love for poetry and writing. Recently, her research on healthcare has provoked her to advocate for a world where healthcare is treated as an inherent right. Driven by a desire to create impactful global change, she blends her interests in economics and social sciences to challenge the "price tag" currently placed on human life. snippet.title: Why You'd Do Anything to Make Them Stay (Even When You Shouldn't)
snippet.description:
Breakups and abandonment triggers can create some of the most overwhelming feelings a person can experience. The fear, panic and despair can feel visceral — as if you won’t cope, can’t survive and would do anything to stop the other person leaving. In this in-depth exploration, CBT Therapist Laura Oates explains why these feelings hit so hard, and how CBT can help you navigate the next 24 hours and beyond.

Laura explores:
• Why abandonment fear feels so intense and “life-or-death”
• The unhelpful behaviours it can trigger — from clinging to shutting down
• How CBT helps you survive the immediate emotional storm
• The CBT model of thoughts, feelings, behaviours and bodily responses
• Automatic Negative Thoughts (ANTs) and how to challenge them
• Capability Affirming Thoughts (CATs) that support you through crisis
• Why breakups reactivate deep attachment patterns
• The evolutionary roots of abandonment fear (“hillside fear”)
• How childhood experiences shape adult attachment styles
• Why insecure attachment leads to repeated painful patterns
• The possibility of “earned secure attachment” in adulthood
• How CBT helps you make changes now while exploring deeper roots over time

This is a compassionate, practical guide for anyone struggling with the intense emotions of abandonment, whether during a breakup or in repeating relationship patterns.

If you are experiencing suicidal thoughts, please contact your GP, call 111, go to A&E, or contact the Samaritans at 116 123.

About Laura Oates
Laura Oates is a Cognitive Behavioural Therapist with extensive experience in anxiety, depression, attachment-related issues and relationship difficulties. She combines evidence-based CBT tools with deep insight into how early experiences shape adult responses, helping clients develop skills for emotional stability, self-trust and healthier relationships.

Have you ever caught yourself drifting into vivid fantasy worlds for hours at a time, only to realize you've lost track of reality? While daydreaming is a normal part of being human, sometimes it can become so immersive that it starts interfering with daily life, relationships, work, or school.

In this video, we'll explore maladaptive daydreaming what it is, why it happens, common signs to look out for, and healthy ways to regain balance. If you've ever wondered whether your imagination has become an escape from overwhelming emotions, stress, loneliness, or trauma, this video may help you better understand your experiences.

Please remember that this video is created for educational purposes only and is not intended to diagnose or replace professional mental health care. If these experiences are causing significant distress or affecting your daily life, consider speaking with a licensed mental health professional.

If this video resonated with you, we'd love to hear your thoughts in the comments. Your experiences may help someone else feel a little less alone.

snippet.title: Signs you have rejection sensitive dysphoria. #shorts
snippet.description:
If a small criticism sends you into an emotional spiral for hours or days, and the intensity surprises even you, there may be a reason for it.

Rejection Sensitive Dysphoria (RSD) is an intense emotional response to perceived rejection or criticism.

A neutral comment can feel like failure. A delayed reply can feel like abandonment. The reaction isn’t about the size of the event—it’s about how the brain interprets it.

This is most often seen in ADHD and in people with histories of emotional invalidation.

The rejection doesn’t have to be real for the pain to feel real.

Understanding this doesn’t erase the reaction—but it can change how you relate to it.

#RSD #ADHD #MentalHealthAwareness #EmotionalRegulation #DrTraceyMarks

Dr Shyamal Mashru is an award-winning psychiatrist and ADHD expert who has treated thousands of people with ADHD.

Drawing on years of clinical experience, he shares one of the most honest and comprehensive conversations we've had about the realities of living with ADHD.
